article.articleHeadline: Six months into an Ebola outbreak in the DRC: they recount life on the front lines against the virus.
article.articleSummary: Six months into an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this piece compiles frontline voices recounting life on the front lines against the virus. Health workers describe grueling shifts in treatment units and isolation wards, constant use of personal protective equipment, and the emotional toll of treating suspected cases amid resource constraints. The narrative highlights infection prevention, contact tracing efforts, urgent patient care decisions, and the challenges of engaging communities to accept containment measures. International and national health partners coordinate with local authorities to sustain surveillance, diagnosis, and patient management, while teams navigate logistical hurdles and risks to staff. The article offers firsthand perspectives on resilience, risk, and the ongoing struggle to control an active Ebola outbreak in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行から6か月：最前線で闘う人々の証言

article.articleHeadline: Saliva test developed to diagnose malaria.
article.articleSummary: Contipharma unveils Smart, the first all-in-one saliva test to diagnose malaria, developed by the Walloon-based company Contipharma. The device integrates sampling, analysis, and result interpretation in a single unit, eliminating finger-prick blood draws and lab processing. It is set to be showcased at Medica in Düsseldorf, Germany, and is aimed chiefly at children and remote communities with limited laboratory access. Validation is underway with the Institut national de recherche biomédicale (INRB) in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo, one of the countries most affected by malaria. Contipharma CEO Bernard Delhez said Kinshasa was chosen to validate the tool to detect the invisible reservoir on the ground where people live, advancing the fight against malaria.

triage.headline_ja: マラリア診断のための唾液検査が開発される
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はマラリア診断用新型唾液検査デバイスの開発・展示に関する技術紹介であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態や疾病発生そのものを報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はベルギーの企業Contipharmaによる新型マラリア唾液検査の開発・検証に関する報道。DRCのキンシャサで検証中との記載はあるが、疾病の発生・流行自体を報じるものではないため、感染症イベントのシグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Document Analysis Reveals Outbreak Response Gaps Across Conflict-Affected
article.articleSummary: Comparative document analysis evaluates outbreak response policy architecture for conflict settings, using 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo. Outbreak was declared a PHEIC on 17 May 2026. Researchers find standing policy instruments rarely assign operational responsibility for conflict outbreak management; provisions are mostly in operational or humanitarian guidance and time-limited plans, not in continental or national health security instruments. Across the analyzed instruments, deficits are pronounced: only a minority receive strong ratings, and a substantial share is entirely absent. Strong ratings are higher in operational guidance and Bundibugyo-specific instruments, but minimal across standing laws, policies, and national plans. Four IHR (2005) monitoring reports contain no strong ratings. Gaps include surveillance for forcibly displaced populations and areas outside state control, and absence of assigned accountability for surveillance and specialized interventions. The study advocates Africa Health Security and Sovereignty Agenda and revisions to IHR/national plans to establish permanent ownership of safeguards.

triage.triage_reason: DRCにおける2026年ブンディブギョ・エボラ出血熱アウトブレイクはPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）として宣言されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進める。
triage.notes: 本記事自体は政策・ガバナンス分析（文書分析研究）であり新規症例データを含まないが、背景となる2026年ブンディブギョ・エボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（PHEIC宣言済み）はIHR・WPRO両基準で高い懸念を示すため、関連する実際のアウトブレイク状況の継続モニタリングとしてPICKUPと判定。

article.articleHeadline: Six months of Ebola in the DRC: between financial burdens, community resistance, and security challenges (By Héritier Matenga) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Six months after the May 15 declaration of the 17th Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the response shows scientific and logistical gains but is constrained by structural obstacles. The Bundibugyo-strain epidemic began in Ituri and spread to North Kivu, surpassing 11,000 cases and over 5,300 deaths as of November. Africa CDC declared a continental public health emergency on May 18. Kinshasa, through the Health Ministry, COUSP, and INSP, coordinated cross-border efforts, but response logistics were hampered by financial and administrative bottlenecks—referred to as the 'Ebola business'—slowing fund disbursement to frontline teams. Community resistance and persistent insecurity in the East (including ADF activity) hinder surveillance and safe burials. Priorities include greater funding transparency, local accountability, and engagement with community leaders, alongside deploying WHO-validated vaccines targeting Bundibugyo. The outbreak echoes the 2018–2020 crisis and underscores enduring zoonotic risks and the need for sustained health-system investment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ出血熱発生から6ヶ月：財政負担、地域社会の抵抗、治安上の課題の狭間で（Héritier Matenga記）- ACP

triage.notes: 発生地域に'Africa'大陸が含まれるが、記事主題はDRC国内（イトゥリ州発生、北キブ州へ拡大）のエボラ流行であり、DRCのみをverified_locationsとした。致死率約48%と極めて高く、治安悪化（ADF活動）や資金配分の遅延など構造的課題が続報監視の重要ポイントとなる。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, the virus was already spreading before the alarm: what lies behind the surge of 11,000 cases VIDEO
article.articleSummary: As of 15 November 2026, an international study published in Science reports that the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo had the virus circulating for weeks before an official alarm was sounded. The researchers note that the rapid spread was driven largely by continuous population movement among communities and across the eastern provinces of the DRC. The article cites a surge of about 11,000 cases linked to this outbreak. The findings suggest that mobility patterns can accelerate Ebola transmission well before surveillance and public health alerts are triggered, underscoring the importance of monitoring infection dynamics in eastern Congo to limit further spread.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Catholic faithful educated on adhering to barrier measures in Isiro - ACP
article.articleSummary: Isiro, Democratic Republic of Congo — Catholic faithful in Isiro-Niangara Diocese, Haut-Uele, were educated on adhering to Ebola barrier measures during a Sunday Eucharistic celebration marking the 11th anniversary of Saint-André-Kaggwa parish in Mendambo. Bishop Dieudonné Madrapile urged abandoning ineffective traditional remedies and urged patients to seek care at the Ebola Treatment Center. He noted alerts extending to Durba, a mining area, highlighting heightened vigilance. Provincial authorities echoed the call: Governor Jean Bakomito urged unwavering vigilance until Ebola is eradicated; Wivine Tongu, provincial Budget Minister, stressed strict observance of barrier measures and ongoing warnings. The article underscores ongoing Ebola risk in northeastern DRC and the role of religious and civil leadership in promoting containment.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola remains an emergency in the Democratic Republic of the Congo — District Policy is now PDNews, news about Politics and Health in the Federal District.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease remains a global health emergency in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with WHO reporting approximately 11,000 infections and over 5,300 deaths across eight provinces. Kenya has begun a 42-day countdown to declare its territory free of the disease, while Nigeria successfully contained an imported episode, illustrating regional vigilance. The WHO urges immediate suspension of disproportionate border closures that hamper economies and outbreak reporting. Laboratory advances include the Ervebo vaccine and new experimental drugs; vaccination is described as a complement to strict isolation, contact tracing, and controlled funeral practices to limit transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Rio de Janeiro records first mpox death in the country
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) death confirmed in Brazil: Rio de Janeiro state reports the country’s first mpox fatality in 2026. Victim resided in Rio de Janeiro city and had a preexisting immunosuppressive condition. By November 13, Rio recorded 382 cases; nationwide Brazil reached 1,009 diagnoses by November 12, with sharp rises since October. Jan 1–Sept 12 accounted for 124 cases, followed by 258 more from Sept 13 onward; positivity rose from 23.6% to 49.5%. About 55 patients required hospitalization; mean age 33.8 years; the capital holds 71.2% of state cases. The 1b variant appears to be gaining traction in Brazil, raising transmission/ severity concerns; the Congo outbreak in 2024 is noted. Symptoms include skin/mucosal lesions, fever, lymphadenopathy, headaches, and myalgias; most cases are mild. MoH allocated 25,000 vaccines on Nov 8; Rio has >2,000 doses for priority groups; two-dose schedule, 28 days apart. Prevention stresses avoiding contact with lesions; treatment is supportive.

article.articleHeadline: Beni: Police enforce Ebola prevention measures in churches.
article.articleSummary: On 15 November 2026, the Congolese National Police (PNC) conducted checks in multiple churches in Beni, North Kivu, to enforce Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention measures amid a continuing health alert. Police visited Catholic, Protestant, and revival churches in areas including Cité Belge and the downtown district to verify compliance with agreed sanitary precautions. Observed measures included handwashing stations at entrances, temperature screening, and physical distancing inside worship spaces. A notable practice required worshippers to wait outside before services to avoid crowding, a rule proposed by the provincial deputy commissioner for support and management. The operation followed an appeal by the provincial police commissioner to church leaders, and the PNC said inspections will continue across public gathering places in Beni to curb transmission of Ebola.

article.articleHeadline: Unprecedented study maps the circulation of Malawi polyomavirus in children in the State of São Paulo.
article.articleSummary: Unprecedented study, published in Nature Communications, maps circulation of Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) in children within the State of São Paulo, Brazil. Using non-targeted metagenomics during SARS-CoV-2 Omicron monitoring, researchers at the Butantan Institute identified MWPyV in 7.7% of 233 pediatric participants aged 1 month to 18 years from the Hospital das Clínicas, Ribeirão Preto, USP. Most detections occurred in children under three years, with low viral loads and symptoms absent in over half, suggesting early-life infection with an indeterminate pathogenic role. The multidisciplinary work combined molecular biology, bioinformatics, and transmission electron microscopy to visualize virions and build a phylogenetic tree, revealing most Brazilian samples as MWPyV genotype I closely related to lineages from Asia, the United States, and Oceania. AlphaFold-based analyses highlighted mutations and stability in structural proteins, including a rare recombination event yielding a mosaic genome. Findings underscore Brazil’s genomic surveillance capacity and the need to monitor emerging viral agents.

article.articleHeadline: Brewery Byproduct Diet Enhances Nile Tilapia Immunity and Cuts Bacterial
article.articleSummary: Streptococcosis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) was mitigated by dietary brewing trub in a Brazilian study from Santa Catarina. Involving 162 juveniles fed for 50 days at 0%, 1%, or 2% trub, followed by an 18-day challenge with intragastric S. agalactiae (1×10^9 CFU/mL). The 1% trub group showed mortality of 2.08%. Growth improved with trub: final weights 60.73 g (1% trub) and 62.77 g (2% trub) vs 47.58 g in controls. Hematology and gut morphology also improved, with higher erythrocyte counts, hematocrit, mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, and intestinal mucosal area. Survival analysis (Mantel-Cox) confirmed significant protection by trub. Brewing trub from Armada microbrewery in São José, Santa Catarina, Brazil, is rich in phenolics (7.23–13.39 mg GAE/g) and may provide a natural immunostimulant alternative to antibiotics in tilapia farming under drug-residue regulations.

article.articleHeadline: Guaíba advises seeking hospital after sporotrichosis progresses.
article.articleSummary: Sporotrichosis outbreak in Guaíba, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. As of 10 November 2026, 293 animals tested positive and 40 people notified (25 confirmed, 9 discarded, 6 under investigation). No hospitalizations; humans receive public care. Animal testing reached 483 exams: 293 positive, 125 negative, 65 awaiting results; about 200 cats on home treatment. Disease is caused by Sporothrix spp. and transmits from animals to humans, with skin lesions that can involve nasal mucosa or internal organs in severe cases. In cats, lesions often affect the muzzle, ears, and paws. Preventive guidance includes gloves and long sleeves when handling soil, plants, or organic material; neutering and indoor housing reduce contact; suspected animals should be isolated, and handlers wear protection. Abandonment of ill animals can sustain the fungus; do not bury carcasses in vacant lots. After May 2024 floods, UCZ operations were strengthened, adding staff, isolation cages, a microscope, medicines, and plans to expand the UCZ cattery.

article.articleHeadline: In figures The Dominican Republic has the lowest incidence of dengue fever among 14 countries and territories in the Americas.
article.articleSummary: Dominican Republic records the lowest dengue incidence among 14 Americas countries/territories in 2026, at 13.21 cases per 100,000. In epidemiological week 42, the country reported 1,534 dengue cases; authorities note increases in La Romana and La Altagracia over four weeks, with 171 cases in week 42, though it isn’t specified whether national total or provincial. Regionally, Brazil leads with 666.67 per 100,000, followed by Bolivia (470.26), Panama (273.19), Peru (255.86), and Ecuador (243.90); Puerto Rico (29.42) and Cuba (16.03) are among the lower, but still above the Dominican Republic. Cumulative totals include Brazil 1,406,184; Colombia 94,618; Peru 83,430; Mexico 69,533; Ecuador 43,350; Venezuela 13,722; Paraguay 11,348; Costa Rica 6,654. PAHO reports 1,914,591 suspected dengue in the Americas in 2026, 605,321 lab-confirmed; 4,059 severe dengue and 655 deaths ( CFR 0.034% ). Week 42 saw 34,572 new suspected cases, 96 severe, 12 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Regional Newspaper: Araçatuba reaches 2,300 dengue cases in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Araçatuba, Brazil, reached 2,307 confirmed cases in 2026, according to a bulletin from Epidemiological Surveillance released on Friday, November 13. The Epidemiological Surveillance historical series, dating back to 1998, shows a concentration in the first half of the year, with March and April reporting 445 and 466 cases and May 353; from June onward, cases declined more sharply. The data indicate a milder year in 2026 compared with 2025, reflecting seasonal patterns and the fluctuating burden of dengue in Araçatuba.

article.articleHeadline: Beware the transition season! Deputy Speaker of the Central Java DPRD warns of PMK threats to livestock.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) threatens livestock in Central Java, Indonesia, as seasonal transition worsens vulnerability. As of 15 November 2026, Deputy Speaker Sarif Abdillah (Banyumas–Cilacap) urges the Central Java Provincial Government to sustain preventive measures against FMD, noting that fluctuating and humid weather during the pancaroba season weakens livestock immunity and facilitates viral growth. He emphasizes routine vaccination of healthy animals, ensuring vaccine stockpiles, and ongoing farm surveillance for early signs. Vaccination is presented as a key control measure to reduce transmission and economic losses, given FMD does not affect humans but devastates livelihoods in the livestock sector. He also calls for expanded collaboration with universities' faculties of veterinary medicine and animal husbandry, and for proactive farmer outreach to promote understanding of each stakeholder's role in prevention and vaccination programs.

triage.triage_reason: 口蹄疫は動物のみに影響し人獣共通感染症ではなく、具体的な発生事例ではなく予防的な注意喚起にとどまるため、公衆衛生上のシグナルとしての基準を満たさない。
triage.notes: 記事は中部ジャワにおける口蹄疫（家畜疾病）への予防的警告であり、人への感染性はないため公衆衛生上のリスクは低い。地方議員による家畜衛生対策の呼びかけであり、具体的な発生報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: New COVID-PJ2.1 Variant Emerges, Doctor Reveals Symptoms That Should Not Be Ignored.
article.articleSummary: New COVID-19 variant COVID-PJ2.1 has emerged in Indonesia amid mutations. While there is no evidence that PJ2.1 is more virulent or increases hospitalizations or deaths, health professionals urge vigilance for symptoms, especially in vulnerable groups. Dr. Ngabila Salama notes COVID-19 is now endemic and mutates every six months to a year, similar to influenza. Symptoms may begin with fever, nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, and cough, and may progress to lower airways with breathlessness. At-risk groups include infants, toddlers, pregnant women, elderly, and those with diabetes, stroke, heart disease, kidney disease, autoimmune diseases, HIV/AIDS, or tuberculosis. Booster vaccination every 6–12 months is recommended; Indovac by Bio Farma is reportedly halted due to stock expiry. Surveillance should be strengthened beyond airports, with puskesmas, ISPA/ILI and SARI programs, PCR testing, and whole-genome sequencing (GISAID). Preventive measures: hand hygiene, masking when ill or in crowds, ventilation, healthy lifestyle, and avoiding self-diagnosis.

triage.headline_ja: 新型COVID変異株PJ2.1が出現、医師が見逃してはいけない症状を明らかに
triage.triage_reason: 新規COVID-19変異株の出現が報告されているが、重症度や感染拡大の増加を示す証拠はなく、現時点では情報不足のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は新変異株の出現と一般的な注意喚起が主旨であり、重症度増加や大規模流行の証拠は示されていない。続報でゲノムサーベイランス結果や症例数の推移を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Sushi Yay customers go viral after complaining of alleged poisoning: 4 ill, 2 taken to the ER.
article.articleSummary: As of 15 November 2026, four people in Jakarta, Indonesia, experienced suspected food poisoning linked to Sushi Yay, Sudirman branch, after dining on an All You Can Eat Ultimate menu and taking leftovers home. One became ill, two required Emergency Department care, and one was hospitalized. The incident, shared on TikTok by the affected diner, led to direct complaints with the restaurant; documents including billing receipts and hospital laboratory results were submitted to support the claim, with the restaurant asking for original documents for reimbursement. Despite private attempts to resolve, the process extended for months, involving visits to the Sudirman outlet and meetings at Sushi Yay’s Jakarta head office. The report does not specify a confirmed pathogen; laboratories conducted tests on treated patients. No information on imported or exported cases is provided.

triage.headline_ja: Sushi Yayの客が食中毒疑いを訴え拡散、4名体調不良のうち2名が救急搬送
triage.triage_reason: 単一レストランでの小規模な食中毒疑い事例であり、病原体も特定されておらず、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: SNS（TikTok）で話題となったが、個別の飲食店における食中毒疑いの消費者苦情であり、公衆衛生イベントとしての広がりは確認されていない。病原体未特定、感染症の公衆衛生危機としての特徴は乏しい。

article.articleHeadline: Is the attack turning into horror again? Infections are rising, deaths are occurring, an outbreak in America after 26 years too, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks are rising in the Americas, with PAHO stripping the United States of its measles-free status as cases surge across several states. In Utah, about 600 cases were recorded (June 2025–June 2026); the US total exceeds 5,400 in 2026, the highest since 1991. Hospitalizations approach 1 in 9, with at least 10 deaths, and most patients were unvaccinated. Measles is highly contagious, with one case potentially seeding 12–18 others and lingering in air for hours. PAHO aims to eradicate 30 diseases by 2030, with measles among them. Bangladesh reports 1,209 suspected deaths (105 confirmed as measles); 1,414 new cases in 24 hours; active cases about 248,060, with 221,539 since March 15 and 212,402 recovered. India records 26,607 cases in July (WHO); Africa has outbreaks in 25 countries; additional hotspots include Indonesia, Pakistan, Yemen, Mexico, Guatemala, Canada, Bolivia, Jordan, Syria, and Europe/Middle East.

triage.headline_ja: 再び恐怖の感染拡大か？感染者増加、死者発生、26年ぶりに米国でもアウトブレイク発生—WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: 世界各地（米国、インド、インドネシア、アフリカ25カ国等）で麻疹の大規模流行が同時多発しており、死亡例・入院例も多数発生。WHO/PAHOが警告を発するなど国際的関心が高く、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は米国・バングラデシュを中心とした世界的な麻疹流行を報じているが、バングラデシュ・パキスタン・イエメン・メキシコ等は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。インドとインドネシアのみ対象国として該当。米国でのPAHO麻疹排除国認定取消し、26年ぶりの大規模流行は特に異常性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Mosquito menace bites hard, Chennai residents call for intensified fogging
article.articleSummary: Chennai faces rising mosquito menace as the monsoon intensifies. City complaints to the civic body reached 1,973 over the last three months, including 301 in the first 13 days of November. Residents urge intensified fogging and door-to-door anti-mosquito measures, noting gaps around Otteri Nullah canal. GCC officials warn mosquito development accelerates in cooler months, while dengue cases have declined: 1,260 in September, 1,174 in October, and 186 up to November 13. They say the current rise may be driven more by Culex mosquitoes in stagnant water than dengue vectors. A pilot of drone-based green pesticide spraying was conducted before the monsoon; authorities plan to spray 240 km of waterways and fog over more than 3,000 km of stormwater drains. About 3,703 personnel are deployed, with 372 hotspots identified and monitored.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊の被害深刻化、チェンナイ住民が燻蒸強化を要望
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数は減少傾向にあり、記事の主題はCulex蚊による不快害虫問題だが、デング熱の継続的な発生状況として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事は蚊（主にCulex種）による不快害虫問題が主題であり、デング熱自体は減少傾向にある。現地当局による対応（燻蒸、ドローン散布等）が進行中であり、国際支援の必要性は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: Wardha News: Dengue outbreak in Kutki; death of a girl; 15 people infected; health concerns come to the fore in a village of 300 people.
article.articleSummary: Kutki, a village of about 300 people in Hinganghat taluka, Wardha district, has 15 dengue cases; an 11-year-old girl Kumud Chandrashankar Shende died a month ago, underscoring health and sanitation concerns. The outbreak coincides with problematic water supply—water is drawn from a river, and villagers say there is no filtration system—raising concerns about drinking-water quality. Authorities are urged to conduct rapid health surveys, screen residents, administer treatment, and carry out fogging/fumigation and preventive measures; villagers ask for a permanent safe drinking-water supply and sanitation improvements. NCP Wardha district president Atul Vandile visited Kutki to assess the situation, offer condolences to the bereaved family, and pledge to secure urgent assistance from the administration.

triage.headline_ja: ワルダー州ニュース：クトキ村でデング熱アウトブレイク、少女死亡、15人感染―人口300人の村で健康不安が表面化
triage.triage_reason: 小規模だが致死例を伴うデング熱クラスター発生であり、衛生・給水問題が継続的な感染リスクとなっているためWPRO基準に複数該当し、地元政治関心も見られる。
triage.notes: 人口300人の村で15例・1死亡と罹患率が高く、未処理の河川水利用による衛生問題が継続している点が懸念材料。地元政治家が行政支援を要請しており、地域レベルでの対応強化が必要とみられる。

article.articleHeadline: E. coli and toxic chemicals found in a borewell in Ujjain: panic over groundwater pollution; risk to kidneys and liver.
article.articleSummary: Groundwater pollution in Ujjain's Parswanath Colony: borewell water tested in a Bhopal laboratory showed E. coli and coliform bacteria along with nickel, cyanide, phenolic compounds, and detergents. Residents accuse pharma and chemical companies in the Devash Road industrial belt of dumping toxic waste into drains, contaminating groundwater and borewells. They had sent samples to a Bhopal lab after not receiving the PCB's report, and are now demanding investigations by the administration and the Pollution Control Board. The discovery raises health concerns: E. coli infection and diarrhea risk; prolonged exposure to chemicals may affect kidneys, liver, and the nervous system, though real risk depends on concentrations and expert assessment. The concern extends to nearby Nagjhiri area, with calls for official testing, wastewater disposal audits, and source identification before attributing responsibility.

triage.headline_ja: ウッジャインの井戸水から大腸菌と有毒化学物質を検出:地下水汚染への懸念、腎臓・肝臓へのリスク
triage.triage_reason: 地下水汚染による大腸菌・化学物質検出は健康リスクがあるが、現時点で人への感染症例報告はなく、環境汚染問題としての性質が強いため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: これは工業廃棄物による地下水汚染が原因の環境汚染問題であり、感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではない。住民による大腸菌・大腸菌群・重金属・化学物質の検出報告であり、人的被害（感染症例）の報告はまだない。地元当局・汚染管理委員会による調査要求が行われている段階。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue and measles are spreading; Kozhikode DMO office without a head.
article.articleSummary: Kozhikode district, Kerala is grappling with dengue, malaria, measles, and chickenpox amid ongoing monsoon rains, while its District Medical Officer (DMO) office is headless. The DMO seat has been vacant since the 26th of last month, and an Additional DMO post remains unfilled; one Additional DMO is currently handling the DMO’s duties. Although Dr. Rajendra has been appointed as the new DMO, he has not yet assumed charge and is based in Thiruvananthapuram; the earlier Additional DMO posted to Kozhikode has moved to Thrissur as DMO, with no replacement for Kozhikode. This leadership vacuum delays outbreak response, including in Anganwadi centers and schools where measles and chickenpox are spreading, and tomato fever is affecting children. As of the 13th of the month, 5 dengue cases were confirmed and 15 suspected; 62 dengue confirmations and 221 suspected since the 1st; 82 measles cases reported by the 13th; malaria and chickenpox cases are rising alongside intermittent rains.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱と麻疹が拡大中、コーリコード地区医療官（DMO）事務所に責任者不在
triage.triage_reason: ケララ州コーリコード地区でデング熱・麻疹・マラリア・水痘が季節性（モンスーン期）に拡大し、行政（DMO）の空白により対応遅延の懸念があるが、重症度や国際的拡大のエビデンスは不明であり、地域内の季節性流行の域を出ない。
triage.notes: 記事は地方紙（Madhyamam, マラヤーラム語）の報道で、季節性感染症（デング熱・麻疹・マラリア・水痘）の増加と地区医療行政（DMO）の人員空白を主題としている。死亡例や重症度の具体的データはなく、国際的拡大のリスクも示唆されていないため、現時点ではWATCHとし続報を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: Calangute locals flag health risk from sewage overflow
article.articleSummary: Calangute, Goa: Residents of a building society along Calangute market lane near Braganca clinic in Naikawaddo report sewage overflow from soak pits contaminating the area and heightening risk of vector-borne diseases. Overflow occurs roughly every 15–30 days, with residents noting dengue and malaria cases linked to the sewage stagnation. They demand early connection to the municipal sewerage pipeline, criticizing a ~15-year delay amid ongoing construction. Sewage tanker use is limited to about 15 trips daily and largely affordable only to hotels/resorts, making it impractical for households. The report highlights a critical public health risk from lacking sewerage infrastructure; no laboratory-confirmed counts are provided. No imported or exported cases are reported. Published 15 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: カランガテ住民、下水溢れによる健康リスクを指摘
triage.triage_reason: 特定地域における下水インフラ問題に起因する住民の懸念に関する地域ニュースであり、検査確認症例数の報告もなく、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地域住民の苦情報道であり、検査確認された症例数や発生規模のデータは記載されていない。インフラ整備の遅延に関する地域社会の関心が中心。

article.articleHeadline: Goa's rabies control model draws interest from Tamil Nadu, Gujarat
article.articleSummary: Goa's rabies control model is drawing interest from Tamil Nadu and Gujarat. Goa became India's first 100% rabies-controlled state in 2021, with no human rabies deaths since 2018 and no cases in 2026. MR-WVS led a delegation headed by Murugan Appupillai to Tamil Nadu and Gujarat to discuss expansion. In Tamil Nadu, officials reportedly favoured statewide rollout over a pilot; final scope and MR-WVS's technical responsibilities await CEO Luke Gamble's approval. In Surat, Gujarat, delegation met deputy CM Harsh Sanghavi and Union Jal Shakti minister CR Patil. Appupillai will present proposals to Gamble during Laos vaccination campaign from Nov 16. Goa's approach combines mass canine vaccination, sterilisation, school education, a 24-hour hotline and rapid response; border dog migration from Maharashtra and Karnataka remains a risk, addressed by border surveillance and coordination. MR-WVS operates in 20 countries and 14 states amid India's National Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination by 2030.

triage.headline_ja: ゴア州の狂犬病制御モデル、タミル・ナードゥ州とグジャラート州が関心
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病対策の成功事例を他州へ展開するという前向きな政策ニュースであり、新規発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はゴア州の狂犬病制御成功モデルを他州（タミル・ナードゥ、グジャラート）へ展開する行政的取り組みに関するもので、感染拡大や新規症例の報告ではない。ラオスでのワクチン接種活動への言及もあるが主題はインド国内の政策展開。

article.articleHeadline: Nipah Review Highlights Placental Viral Crossing While Human Vertical
article.articleSummary: Nipah virus, an enveloped, negative-sense ssRNA paramyxovirus (Henipavirus), is an urgent WHO priority with case fatality estimates of 40–90%. Since its 1998–1999 Malaysia–Singapore outbreak, Nipah has caused recurrent outbreaks, with Bangladesh and India as major foci. Zoonotic spillover arises from Pteropus medius fruit bats, notably via raw date palm sap or contaminated fruit; human-to-human spread occurs through contact with bodily fluids or respiratory droplets. A Frontiers in Public Health review synthesizes clinical, epidemiological, and animal data, noting experimental infections show placental barrier breach and fetal infection, but human vertical transmission remains unconfirmed virologically. The ~18.2 kb genome encodes six proteins (N, P, M, F, G, L). Initial replication in respiratory epithelium disseminates to endothelium, causing vasculitis and multi-organ involvement (lungs, brain, heart, spleen, kidneys). Pregnancy may amplify risk due to gestational immune shifts and reduced cardiopulmonary reserve; animal models support placental crossing.

triage.headline_ja: ニパウイルスレビュー：胎盤バリア通過を強調する一方、ヒトにおける垂直感染は未確認
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は学術レビュー論文（病態生理・胎盤感染メカニズム）の紹介であり、新規の発生事例や症例報告ではないため、トリアージ対象のシグナルには該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は過去の疫学的知見（1998-99年マレーシア・シンガポール流行、バングラデシュ・インドでの再発）を背景としたレビュー論文の紹介であり、現在進行中の新規発生事例ではないため、具体的な発生国としての列挙は該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue: Infections have doubled for various reasons, but it's reassuring, say health officials.
article.articleSummary: Dengue infections in Siliguri and Darjeeling district, West Bengal, have more than doubled this year, reaching 215 cases to date, though officials say the surge is not as severe as in 2022 when over 700 people were infected across the same area. Despite multiple adverse conditions and gaps in prevention programs, the authorities remain comparatively reassured about the current outbreak and warn of renewed risk next year. January–May are considered crucial for prevention through door-to-door awareness, source reduction, and larval surveillance, but electoral duties kept some staff preoccupied. Administrative disruptions in Siliguri Municipality, including the mayor's resignation and drainage-cleaning lapses, compounded control efforts. Deputy CMHO-2 Dr. Anowar Hossain notes that atypical rainfall—short bursts followed by dry spells—created mosquito-friendly stagnation in several areas. Officials anticipate a drop in cases with winter, but stress intensified preventive measures from early next year.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱：様々な要因で感染者数が倍増も、安心できる状況と保健当局
triage.triage_reason: 西ベンガル州シリグリ地域でデング熱症例が倍増しているが、2022年ピーク時より少なく、当局は制御可能と評価しており、重大な公衆衛生上の緊急性は低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 地域のデング熱の季節的増加に関する報道で、当局は制御可能と評価。例年の変動範囲内であり、国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Bacteria attached to tilapia (Luo-fei fish) "could kill within 72 hours" Shenzhen, China
article.articleSummary: Vibrio vulnificus infection linked to tilapia exposure reported in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. A 69-year-old man sustained a puncture wound on his right palm while filleting tilapia (Luo-fei fish). The wound seemed minor, but three days later he developed a fever up to 39°C, marked swelling of the right hand, blistering on the dorsum, and limited hand movement. Hospitalized, initial suspicion pointed to V. vulnificus infection; after several days of antibiotics, he was transferred to Shenzhen Third People's Hospital for intensive care. High-throughput genetic testing confirmed Vibrio vulnificus as the causative pathogen. Following 16 days of treatment, fever resolved, inflammation markers declined, and he was discharged. Experts warn V. vulnificus has a very high fatality rate if not treated promptly: mortality can exceed 50% within 48 hours of infection and rise toward 100% if treatment is delayed beyond 72 hours.

triage.headline_ja: ティラピア（ロウフェイ魚）に付着した細菌が「72時間以内に死亡の恐れ」中国・深圳
triage.triage_reason: 単一症例であり、ヒト-ヒト感染のリスクがない環境由来（魚介類接触）感染症のため、公衆衛生上の緊急性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 本症例は魚の捌き作業中の創傷感染によるビブリオ・バルニフィカス感染で、1例の個別症例報告。治療により回復しており、アウトブレイクやヒト-ヒト感染の兆候はない。

article.articleHeadline: Risk of a severe infection: the 'slimming' injections from China turned out to be contaminated with bacteria.
article.articleSummary: Contaminated slimming injections from Shanghai ERP Peptide Biotechnology (China) carry dangerous bacteria capable of causing severe infections. Laboratory findings identified Acinetobacter seifertii, Acinetobacter nosocomialis, and Cutibacterium acnes in the products. Health Canada warned that administration of contaminated injectable preparations may require hospitalization and can lead to life-threatening sepsis. Canada has seized more than 11,400 vials from a supplier and two online sellers; the outlets halted operations after regulator intervention. The warning covers products containing retatrutidom, tirzepatide, MOTS-C and NAD+, which were not approved for sale in Canada and have not been evaluated by Health Canada for safety or efficacy. SHOT PROVERKA notes similar substances are offered by Russian online shops, marketed for weight loss and rejuvenation.

triage.triage_reason: 中国製の未承認注射製品が複数の病原細菌に汚染されている事例だが、ヒト-ヒト感染や実際の感染症例発生の報告はなく、製品規制・流通問題としての側面が強いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本事例は自然発生の感染症アウトブレイクではなく、未承認の美容・痩身注射製品が細菌汚染されていたことによる健康リスク事案。中国（上海）の製造企業が発生源とされるが、実際の感染症例発生報告は本文中に明記されておらず、カナダの規制当局による製品押収・警告が中心。ロシア・カナダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Pediatric Inpatient Influenza Detections Correlated Positively With
article.articleSummary: Influenza type and subtype dynamics in southern China were evaluated in a 65-month retrospective study of pediatric inpatient tests. Using 21,965 throat-swab records from 17,835 inpatients aged 0–14 with lower respiratory tract infections (Jan 2021–May 2026), overall positivity was 2.51% for A(H1N1)pdm09, 3.34% for A(H3N2), and 2.18% for influenza B. The leading influenza category changed across five calendar years, but within each year crude and age-standardized positivity identified the same dominant type. Multivariable models showed age effects varied by virus; compared with infants <1 year, children aged 6–14 had adjusted odds ratios of 1.58 for A(H1N1)pdm09, 5.94 for A(H3N2), and 4.23 for influenza B. Temporal concordance with the Chinese National Influenza Center regional surveillance in southern China was strong (Pearson r 0.765 for H1N1, 0.662 for H3N2, 0.895 for B across 47 months), with 35 of 44 months sharing the same leading category (Cohen’s κ 0.693). Conclusion: routine inpatient testing can supplement regional surveillance by providing localized, age-stratified influenza data.

article.articleHeadline: City CDC experts remind: When using these facilities in public places, guard against bacterial and fungal contamination.
article.articleSummary: As of November 15, 2026, Qingdao City Center for Disease Control and Prevention warns that public venues such as hotels, malls, spa facilities, and gyms carry bacterial and fungal contamination risks. Shared hotel slippers can transmit dermatophytes, notably Trichophyton rubrum, causing athlete’s foot (tinea pedis) and, with stubborn fungi, onychomycosis. To mitigate, use disposable nonwoven slippers or bring your own; if using public slippers, rinse and wash feet promptly after wearing. Public wet floors in hotel showers, pools, or gym areas sustain fungi and skin infections; HPV strains 1–4 can cause plantar warts in moist, warm conditions. Always wear waterproof footwear in these areas. Hand dryers in public toilets may disperse bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella, Staphylococcus aureus) and fail to sterilize them; wipe hands with paper towels or air-dry away from dryers. Practical tips: avoid direct contact with public items; don’t go barefoot with foot injuries; and refuse hand-dryer use.

article.articleHeadline: Short term effects of ambient air pollution exposure on influenza: a multi-city study in Shandong, China
article.articleSummary: Short-term exposure to major air pollutants increases influenza-like illness (ILI) risk in Shandong Province, China, based on 2015–2019 data from 16 cities, totaling 2,145,543 ILI cases. Except for ozone (O3), all six major pollutants show positive associations with ILI using city-specific quasi-Poisson DLNM and meta-analysis. NO2 (CRR 1.041, 95% CI 1.031–1.052) and SO2 (CRR 1.040, 95% CI 1.023–1.058) exhibit the strongest effects. O3 is inversely associated with ILI. Risks are higher among children aged 5–14, during transition seasons (spring and autumn), and in coastal areas. Meta-regression indicates that higher gross domestic product and denser healthcare resources mitigate these pollutant-associated risks, while basin topography exacerbates them during severe pollution episodes. Findings support localized, resource-adjusted air quality early warning systems to protect vulnerable populations from pollution-related ILI.

article.articleHeadline: A Child's Own Words: Measles Resurges - 20261116
article.articleSummary: Measles remains a global threat despite vaccine success. The piece recalls long measles histories in Hong Kong, Japan, and the Americas, noting Indigenous populations in the Americas had no prior immunity and suffered devastating outbreaks; a 1532 epidemic across Mexico to the Andes killed many. It emphasizes measles’ high contagion and severe complications, especially in infants, and tracks how vaccines transformed control: first US vaccine in 1963; MMR in 1971; WHO Expanded Program on Immunization in 1974; the US declared elimination of endemic transmission in 2000. Yet in 2024, about 11 million global infections and 95,000 deaths occurred, concentrated in under-vaccinated regions. The piece flags anti-vaccine misinformation, citing Andrew Wakefield and Robert F. Kennedy Jr.; Texas recorded two measles deaths in 2025, after which Kennedy Jr. softened his stance though public trust remains low. The message: the measles-elimination battle continues.

article.articleHeadline: Quarantine Headquarters issues a risk advisory for highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI)
article.articleSummary: Nov 13, 2026: Korea's Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA) issued a High-Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) risk advisory as domestic poultry outbreaks rise and wild birds test positive for H5N1 and H5N9. Since Oct 12, HPAI antigens were detected in wild birds at Suncheon Bay, with a total of 10 detections to date, and six poultry-farm outbreaks: Yeoncheon and Yeoju (Gyeonggi Province) layer farms; Jangheung (Jeollanam-do) fattening duck farm; Ganghwa (Incheon) layer farm; Jincheon (Chungcheongbuk-do) breeding duck farm; and Paju (Gyeonggi) quail farm. Migratory-bird tracking shows a mallard moving south from Baicheng, Jilin, China, arriving in Uljin, North Gyeongsang, by Nov 7. In Japan, HP AI antigens were detected in wild birds/environments in Akita, Hokkaido, Kagoshima, with suspected cases in Kyoto (200,000-layer) and Chiba (40,000-layer) farms. Measures include two-stage farm-vehicle disinfection, PPE and dedicated footwear, closing back doors without anterooms, entry disinfection, hand hygiene, and intensified central inspections.

article.articleHeadline: Thai dengue toll at 47 as southern Region 11 reports 1.7 times national level
article.articleSummary: Thailand reports 34,875 dengue cases and 47 deaths nationwide through November 7, 2026, with a southern outbreak driving higher local numbers. The published data show Health Regions 11 and 12 in southern Thailand recording the highest case counts, with Region 11 at roughly 1.7 times the national level. Flooding and standing water are cited as potential drivers of transmission via Aedes mosquitoes, prompting the government to mobilize health workers and village volunteers to raise dengue awareness and help communities prepare. Most infections affect school- or working-age individuals; deaths are concentrated among older adults. Despite the south surge, the 2026 national total remains below the 2025 level. August was the peak reporting period, about 1,450 cases, compared with roughly 2,700 in 2025. Officials emphasize prevention, surveillance, and community engagement to curb further spread.

article.articleHeadline: Southern Thailand faces dengue warning amid flooding, 47 deaths
article.articleSummary: Southern Thailand faces elevated dengue risk as flooding and persistent rainfall expand Aedes mosquito breeding sites. The Thai government reports 34,875 dengue fever cases and 47 deaths nationwide between January 1 and November 7, with the total number of cases this year still below 2025. A warning issued on November 15 cites Department of Disease Control figures. Dengue burden is highest in Health Regions 11 (Surat Thani, Ranong, Phuket, Phang Nga, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Chumphon, Krabi) and 12 (Trang, Narathiwat, Pattani, Phatthalung, Yala, Songkhla, Satun); Health Region 11 records about 1.7 times the national average. Most patients are schoolchildren and working-age adults; deaths are concentrated among the elderly. Peak monthly cases reached about 1,450 in August. Authorities urge health workers and volunteers to raise awareness about standing water and breeding sites and prepare for possible further infections in flood-affected southern communities, aiming to prevent a rise in cases.

article.articleHeadline: Thailand's Dengue Cases and Deaths Put Prevention in Focus
article.articleSummary: Thailand reports 34,875 dengue infections and 47 deaths nationwide through Nov 7, 2026, with southern Health Region 11 recording transmission at 1.7 times the national average amid flood-driven mosquito breeding. Floodwaters in the Gulf of Thailand monsoon fuel late-season outbreaks; national infections peaked in August at about 1,450, versus 2,700 in August 2025. School-age children and working-age adults account for most cases, while older adults experience deadlier outcomes due to underlying conditions; officials have mobilized village health volunteers to clear larval habitats before floodwaters recede. Early dengue mimics flu; symptoms include fever 39–40 C, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle aches, and nausea. Red-flag signs—vomiting, abdominal pain, skin bleeding, nosebleeds, dark stools—require emergency care. Prevention centers on eliminating standing water weekly, repairing screens, sleeping under nets, and using DEET/picaridin. Travelers should monitor weekly provincial advisories.

article.articleHeadline: Northern Ghana Surveillance Finds High Malaria Positivity Among Tested
article.articleSummary: Malaria in pregnancy positivity rate in Northern Region, Ghana, was 46.8% (95% CI 46.3–47.2) among 112,510 tested of 120,535 suspected presentations from 2020–2024, based on routine health surveillance. Testing occurred for 93% of suspected cases. Age-specific analyses showed pregnant women aged 35 years and older had an 18% lower positivity rate than adolescents (adjusted positivity rate ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.89; p=0.000). Geographic analysis identified 14 districts with significantly higher positivity than the Tamale Metropolis baseline. Although annual positivity trended upward from 2020 to 2024, the year-to-year change was not statistically significant. The findings confirm malaria in pregnancy remains highly endemic in the Northern Region, Ghana, with marked age and district disparities, prompting intensified, targeted interventions—especially for adolescent pregnant women and high-burden districts—to accelerate elimination. Analyses used descriptive statistics and crude/adjusted Poisson regression of District Health Information Management System 2 data.

article.articleHeadline: Urine FujiLAM II Test Shows High Specificity but Limited Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Vietnam multicentre evaluation of FujiLAM II urine LAM assay for pulmonary TB finds high specificity (99.3%) but limited overall sensitivity (~29–30%) across 3,087 adults in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Background: 2024 TB burden included 10.7 million cases, 1.23 million deaths, and about 2.4 million undiagnosed. In facility-based case-finding (n≈1,546), sensitivity 30.8% with 98.4% specificity; in community-based active case-finding (n≈1,541), sensitivity 6.5% with 99.9% specificity. Using sputum culture as primary reference in 2,217 participants yielded 30.5% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity; against the full microbiological reference standard, 29.5% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity. Among people living with HIV (n=684), sensitivity rose to 52.9% with 98.4% specificity; HIV-negative participants had 27.1% sensitivity and 99.6% specificity. FujiLAM II, designed to improve reproducibility and reduce costs versus FujiLAM I, shows high specificity but limited case-finding yield, especially in asymptomatic community cohorts. Trials conducted June 2024–June 2025.

article.articleHeadline: Dozens of Russians Fall Ill: Mysterious Virus Outbreak Forces Vladimir Putin to Act.
article.articleSummary: Dozens of Russian tourists in the Vietnamese coastal city of Nha Trang have fallen ill with an unidentified infection characterized by high fever, severe headache, runny nose, and a persistent, severe cough; local doctors have not identified the pathogen. Russia's Rospotrebnadzor has opened an investigation, requesting data from Vietnam's health ministry and the Russian tour-operator association. No definitive diagnosis yet; authorities warn it could be a novel pathogen or a known variant, with symptoms resembling influenza-like illness and possible seasonal respiratory infections. The outbreak follows earlier pest-related fears in Siberia and a Coxsackie virus outbreak among Russian tourists in Vietnam. Russian tourism officials and diplomats attempt to downplay the situation; no consular inquiries reported in Ho Chi Minh City. Lab results from Hanoi are awaited. Published 2026-11-15.

article.articleHeadline: Ministry of Agriculture: Since 2024, nearly 500,000 doses of African swine fever vaccine have been administered.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam reports vaccination of African swine fever (ASF) in domestic pigs under the Agriculture Department’s vaccination program; since 2024, 499,008 of 500,000 allocated doses have been administered across seven provinces and 54 farms through the first half of 2026. Danlu Province vaccinated the most pigs (287,620), followed by Des East Coast Province (92,021) and Brakan Province (88,107); additional covered provinces include Lechak, Naihu, Kishun, and Bangbanha. Despite vaccination, ASF outbreaks persisted in 236 communities across 23 provinces as of October 22, 2026. The government has re-designated 716 cities/towns as buffer or monitoring zones. The Animal Industry Bureau approved a Vietnam-developed ASF vaccine for commercial sale, accelerating rollout, and the Agriculture Department plans to import vaccines from Korea and the United States by 2027 to broaden protection.

article.articleHeadline: Are you planning a trip to these countries? A dangerous disease is taking hold, the number of infected has jumped by as much as 53 percent.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is rising in popular destinations, notably Vietnam, Mexico, and the Dominican Republic, with increases in Mexico, Bolivia, Peru, and Colombia up to 53% in four weeks. By week 40 the Dominican Republic reported 415 cases; Honduras had over 12,000 by end-October. Bangladesh records about 136,930 cases with 427 deaths this year, while Vietnam reports 131,205 infections, up 37% from last year. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes; incubation is 4–10 days. Four serotypes exist; prior infection can raise the risk of severe disease on reinfection. Symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, and muscle pains; warning signs include severe abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, and circulatory problems. Vaccination guidance varies: STIKO recommends vaccination for those previously infected, while BCRT’s Thomas Jelinek advocates vaccination even for those without prior infection; two doses, spaced at least three months. Europe with Aedes mosquitoes may see transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Four-year-old latest dengue fatality in Iloilo
article.articleSummary: Dengue fatality in Iloilo City, Philippines: a four-year-old boy from the City Proper district died on Oct 29 from complications of dengue after fever began on Oct 26 and initial at-home treatment. Late consultation was cited as a factor; health officials note dengue testing is available at city health centers even on day one, using the dengue duo test with results in 15-20 minutes. Residents are urged to seek care for fever, as early detection and monitoring enable hydration and treatment. As of Nov 7, Iloilo City recorded 844 dengue cases, up 46.8% from 575 in the same period last year, and nine deaths (three times 2025's period). No outbreak is declared yet, with thresholds being assessed against the 2021-2025 average of 1,004 cases, an attack rate of 182.66 (five-year average 190.74), and a case fatality rate of 1.07%.
